introHtml:
If you own land around McGregor, you already know this corner of McLennan County is changing fast. The SpaceX test facility south of town has brought jobs, traffic, and a wave of land buyers who want their places fenced right. Whether you run cows on a section of blackland or you just bought 30 acres off US 84, Brazos Ridge Fence Co. builds fence that holds up to this ground and this weather.

We're a Waco-based crew that works southwest McLennan County every week. We know where the rock starts, where the clay swells, and where the Middle Bosque bottoms will test a water gap every spring. Call (254) 555-0184 for a free written estimate, or start with our ranch fence cost guide if you're still penciling out the numbers.

sections.heading: Fence Work on Southwest McLennan County Ground
sections.html:
The land around McGregor isn't all the same, and your fence bid shouldn't be either. East of town you're mostly in blackland clay that swells and shrinks with every wet spell, so we set corners deep and brace them heavy. West toward Crawford and the Coryell line, the limestone gets shallow, and driving t-posts turns into drilling. We bring the right equipment for both instead of guessing.

Creek bottoms are the other big factor out here. The Middle Bosque and the smaller draws that feed it will flood hard after a spring storm, and a standard fence across a crossing just becomes debris. We build swinging water gaps and flood-rated crossings so one gully washer doesn't take out a quarter mile of your fence.

If your place straddles the county line or sits closer to Crawford or Valley Mills, we cover that ground too. Same crew, same pricing, same written estimate.

sections.heading: McGregor Land Is Changing, and Fences Are Part of It
sections.html:
The SpaceX facility has done for McGregor what nobody saw coming twenty years ago. Land that used to trade quiet is getting bought, split, and improved, and good fence is usually the first improvement on the list. New owners want clean property lines, secure perimeters, and entrances that look like somebody cares about the place.

We work both sides of that change. For working cattle operations, we build and rebuild the barbed wire and net wire that keeps stock where it belongs. For newer buyers, we do full perimeter packages, pipe fencing along the road frontage, and entrance gates that set the tone for the whole property.

Either way, you get a written estimate up front with real per-foot numbers, not a vague range that grows once the work starts. We're licensed and insured, and we show up when we say we will.

sections.heading: What Ranch Fencing Costs Near McGregor
sections.html:
Here are honest ballpark numbers for this area. Five-strand barbed wire usually runs about $2.50 to $4.00 per foot, which puts a mile of perimeter fence in the range of $13,000 to $21,000 depending on terrain, corners, and gates. Net wire for sheep, goats, or mixed stock runs a little more.

Pipe fence generally lands between $30 and $50 per foot depending on pipe size and spacing, and high game fence runs about $4.50 to $8.00 per foot. Rocky ground west of McGregor adds drilling time, and that shows up in the bid, so we walk your lines before we quote anything.

Every job gets a free written estimate with the price broken out by the foot. For a deeper look at what drives these numbers, read our ranch fence cost guide or call (254) 555-0184 and we'll talk through your project.

faq.q: Do you build fence on properties near the SpaceX facility in McGregor?
faq.a: Yes, we fence land all around southwest McLennan County, including properties near the test facility south of town. A lot of our recent McGregor work has come from owners improving land in that area. We handle everything from barbed wire perimeters to pipe fence and entrance gates.

faq.q: How much does a mile of barbed wire fence cost around McGregor?
faq.a: For a typical five-strand barbed wire fence, most McGregor jobs land between $13,000 and $21,000 per mile. The spread depends on terrain, how many corners and gates you need, and whether we're driving posts into clay or drilling into rock. We walk your lines first and give you a free written estimate with exact per-foot pricing.

faq.q: Can you set posts in the rocky ground west of McGregor?
faq.a: We can. The limestone gets shallow between McGregor and the Coryell County line, and driven t-posts alone won't cut it there. We bring drilling equipment and set posts in rock the right way, so your fence stays tight instead of leaning over after the first wet winter.

faq.q: What if my cattle get out through a damaged fence near McGregor?
faq.a: Call our 24/7 emergency line at (254) 555-0184. Cattle out on US 84 or FM roads around McGregor is a serious liability, so we treat it as urgent. We'll get a crew out to patch the break and secure your stock, then quote the permanent repair.
